title: smtp: messages without Message-ID accepted then silently lost during NNTP injection
description:
Why: The SMTP DATA handler never checks for a Message-ID header. A message without one is accepted with 250, queued, and delivered to the SMTP store — but when the NNTP injection path (nntp_client.rs) forwards it to the NNTP reader, the reader rejects it with 441 Missing Message-ID header. The sender got a 250 OK but the article never reaches Usenet. Silent data loss.

What: In the SMTP DATA handler, after dot-unstuffing and before enqueuing, check whether the message contains a Message-ID header. If absent, either:
  (a) synthesize one (format: <timestamp.random@config.hostname>) and prepend it, or
  (b) reject with 554 5.6.0 Missing Message-ID header.
Option (a) matches RFC 5321 §6.4 guidance for submission servers that fix up messages; option (b) is stricter. Decide which is appropriate for the submission use case and document the choice.
